newsitem.title: UK: Compel buys Hamilton, makes cash call.
newsitem.headline: Compel buys Hamilton, makes cash call.

text.p: Compel Group Plc, a UK-based corporate systems intergrator, said on Wednesday it had bought Hamilton Rentals Group Ltd for a maximum consideration of 14.54 million stg.
It also said it planned to raise about 15.19 million stg through an 11-for-18 rights issue at 160p a share.

Compel said it bought Hamilton, a short-term computer rental company and a corporate systems reseller, with an initial consideration of 13.69 million stg and will pay another 850,000 stg after the year ending June 30 1997, depending on Hamilton's financial performance.
"The enlarged group will remain focused on corporate customers and will materially benefit from its increased size, breadth and coverage," said Neville Davis, chairman and chief executive of Compel.
The rights issue is being underwritten by Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull Securities Ltd, the company said.
David Frankling would join the board of Compel while remaining managing director of Hamilton, it said.

Hamilton made operating profit of 1.3 million stg on turnover of 17.6 million stg for the six months ended June 30 1996, following an operating profit of 2.1 million on turnover of 31.2 million stg for the year ended December 31 1995.
